title: Return proven prefix-only selector ranges without residual scans
masterplan_authority: Revision 11 / Version 2.2.0 / Gate 1 — Renovation and owner-directed Genesis
finding: TensorView.select() already consumes a contiguous leading selector prefix and proves its exact candidate interval with bisect_left/bisect_right. When that prefix contains every requested selector, the remaining normalized selector map is empty, but the implementation still entered matching_entries(), walked every entry in the proven interval, evaluated all() over an empty predicate set, and rematerialized the result. A prefix covering the complete TensorView therefore performed a redundant full-range traversal after its bounds were already established.
primary_claim: TensorView.select() now returns immediately when canonical bisect bounds have consumed every selector. A full-range prefix reuses the existing immutable entries tuple, while a proper prefix-only subrange materializes only the already-proven interval without executing residual predicates. Queries with genuine non-prefix predicates keep the existing residual fail-closed filtering path.
gardener_decision: Reuse the existing canonical bisect bounds and immutable entries tuple. Do not add an entry index, cache, selector result cache, planner, alternate Tensor representation, or second filtering abstraction. Once normalized is empty after prefix consumption, return the proven range directly; keep the existing matching_entries loop only for genuine residual selectors.
